parameters.content:
## Personalised outreach videos for a whole lead list

Every lead row with an empty `Status` becomes its own ~12 second 1920x1080
video — their first name, their company, their logo, their role — and the
whole list goes up as **ONE Zvid bulk render**. When the batch finishes,
each video's URL is written back to that lead's row.

### Setup (about five minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*,
   *Submit bulk render* and *Get batch status*.
2. **Google Sheets** — attach your Google Sheets credential to
   *Read leads sheet* AND *Write URLs back*, then pick your spreadsheet and
   tab in BOTH nodes.
3. Give the sheet this header row (exact names):
   `FirstName | Company | Website | LogoUrl | Role | Status | VideoUrl`
4. **Open Config** and make it yours: `senderName`, `senderTitle`,
   `senderCompany`, `senderLogoUrl`, `brandColor`, the three `pitchPoints`,
   `ctaText` and `meetingUrl`.
5. **Run it — this renders for real.** `dryRun` is `false` out of the box, so
   the first run spends credits: **12 per lead**, i.e. ~120 for a full batch
   of 10. Afterwards click **▶ Watch video** to play them inside n8n, one
   item per lead.
   *Want a free look first?* Set `dryRun: true` in Config and run once: you
   get the exact per-video and whole-batch cost plus an **editorLink** that
   opens the first lead's video in the editor, with nothing charged.
6. **Free plans cap a bulk request at 5 items** — set `maxPerRun` to 5 there,
   or raise it on a paid plan. Overflow leads are reported as
   `leftForNextRun` and picked up on the following run.
7. **Activate** for the weekly schedule (Tuesdays, 9am).

## Your sheet is the queue

| FirstName | Company | Website | LogoUrl | Role | Status | VideoUrl |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

- **`Status` empty** → the lead is waiting for a video. After a successful
  render the row gets `done` + the video URL. Clear `Status` to re-record.
- **Required:** `FirstName` and `Company`. Rows missing either are skipped
  with a named reason in the run output — one bad row never sinks the batch.
- **`LogoUrl` is optional.** Leave it empty (or point it at something that is
  not an image) and the lead gets a **monogram chip** instead: the first
  letter of their company on a tint derived from the company's name. When you
  do have one, use a plain `https://…` URL — a transparent PNG or an SVG on a
  light background looks best, since it sits on a white card.
- **`Website`** is optional and shows as a small domain caption under the
  lead's logo. **`Role`** is optional too: it becomes the *written with a …
  in mind* line, which falls back to *written for the team at …*.
- More pending leads than `maxPerRun`? The overflow is reported as
  `leftForNextRun` and handled on the next run.

## What is personalised, and what is not

*Build bulk request* produces ONE template plus one small `variables` set
per lead — that is what makes the whole list a single API call.

| Per lead (from the sheet) | Shared (from Config) |
| --- | --- |
| First name, company, website | Sender name/title/company + logo |
| Logo **or** monogram chip | Brand colours, both fonts |
| Role line | The three pitch points |
| Type sizes that fit their name | CTA text + meeting link |

- **Type scales to the data.** The greeting steps 128 → 50 px so a 24
  character first name still sets on one line, and both growing blocks are
  bottom-anchored, so an extra line grows upward instead of colliding.
- **Every sheet value is HTML-escaped**, so a company called
  `Sable & Wren <Holdings>` renders as text instead of breaking the markup.
- *Check lead logos* HEADs each `LogoUrl` first: a dead link, a non-image or
  an oversized file quietly becomes a monogram instead of a failed render.
  A CDN that refuses HEAD (405) is trusted, not punished.
- No stock footage and no video elements at all — just type, the two logos
  and a soft music bed, which is why it does not look like an ad.

## Dry run — the free preview, opt-in

**`dryRun` is `false` by default**, so a normal run renders for real and
spends credits (~12 per lead). These two nodes stay dark unless you turn the
dry run on.

Set `dryRun: true` in **Config** to take the free pass instead: it validates
the first lead's resolved video, quotes the exact cost (per video AND for the
whole batch), lists every lead with whether it will use a logo or a monogram,
and saves that first video as a **draft** — the output carries an
`editorLink` like `https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open it, watch the video, tweak Config, then set `dryRun` back to `false`.
Saving a draft costs nothing, and the sheet is not touched on a dry run.

## One request, N videos — how the bulk API behaves

- The whole batch goes up as **one** `POST /api/render/bulk/api-key` call: a
  single shared payload plus one small `variables` set per lead. Zvid
  resolves and validates every item, then queues one render job each.
- **Per-item validation is best-effort**: a bad lead is rejected
  *individually* (reported in `rejected`) while the rest of the batch renders.
- Credits are reserved **per job** and refunded automatically for failed
  renders. The whole batch is rejected up-front if your balance cannot cover
  it — the 402 names the exact total.
- Poll `GET /api/render/bulk/{id}` until `bulk.status` leaves `processing`.
  Job **names are NULL until a job completes**, so this workflow maps results
  by jobId, never by name.
- A timeout here does **not** cancel anything — renders finish server-side and
  show up at https://app.zvid.io. `timeoutMinutes` is 30 because ten videos
  share the queue; raise it for longer lists.

## Sending them (optional tail)

The required path stops with a video URL in every lead row — deliberately, so
the import runs with a Zvid key and a Google account and nothing else. To
send, extend after *Run summary* (one item per lead, each with `videoUrl`,
`firstName`, `company`):

- **Email** — a Gmail / Microsoft Outlook / Send Email node. Put the video
  **as a link** in the body, never as an attachment: a 1 MB MP4 attachment is
  a spam-filter magnet, and a link lets you see who watched.
- **LinkedIn / sequencer** — pass `videoUrl` to Lemlist, Instantly, Smartlead
  or HeyReach over their HTTP API as a custom variable on the lead.
- **CRM** — write `videoUrl` back onto the HubSpot/Pipedrive contact so the
  rep can send it by hand.

### Feeding it from a CRM instead of a sheet

Replace *Read leads sheet* with a HubSpot / Apollo / Salesforce node and map
their fields onto the same column names (`FirstName`, `Company`, `Website`,
`LogoUrl`, `Role`) — everything downstream is unchanged. Keep a write-back
step so the same lead is not recorded twice.

## ▶ Watch video

Click this node after a run to watch the finished videos **inline** — n8n
renders each downloaded `video/mp4` binary as a player with a download
button. **One item per lead.**

It never fails a run: `onError: continueRegularOutput` plus 3 retries,
because the CDN can 404 for a moment right after a render completes. The
sheet and *Run summary* already carry every URL by this point.

## Official Zvid nodes

These HTTP Request nodes are deliberately core-only so the workflow imports
untouched anywhere, including n8n Cloud.

On self-hosted n8n you can install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**
(Settings → Community nodes) and swap:

| HTTP Request node | Native replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Validate project (free) | **Zvid** → Render → Validate |
| Submit bulk render | **Zvid** → Render → Create Bulk |
| Get batch status + Wait | **Zvid Trigger** (render webhook) |

The Zvid Trigger removes the polling loop entirely.
